Subject: Hosted billing units — quick clarification request

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to picking a vendor and wanted to validate how billing units will map to our usage patterns before we run final numbers. A couple quick questions:

1) For the Hosted API, how do Chat Completions vs Responses endpoints differ in billing units? We have a mix of streaming and non-streaming calls.
2) Is the legacy /completions endpoint billed the same way as Responses, or does it still follow the old token buckets?
3) Do streaming responses incur the same per-token compute pricing or is there an additional streaming surcharge?

We estimate 25M input tokens and 40M output tokens per month across several models. If you can point to the rate card lines or a one-page mapping, that'd be a big help for our procurement and forecasting.

Hi Alex — great questions, thanks for sending the numbers. High level: the Hosted API normalizes billing around the Responses surface, but there are a few important distinctions to call out so forecasting is accurate. Short answers first, details below.

Quick answers:
- Responses is our canonical pricing surface for most new models (per-input-token + per-output-token) — use this for baseline compute units.
- Chat Completions is mapped onto Responses for billing, but chat-style streaming and function/tool-calling can change effective units due to prefix reuse and streaming token accounting.
- Legacy /completions still appears on invoices for older integrations and follows the historical token mapping; new hosted customers should model as Responses unless you keep legacy endpoint calls.
- No separate streaming surcharge in the rate card — streaming changes how tokens are counted and whether prefix/KV cache reduces billed input tokens, which affects unit counts.

I'll attach the ratecard excerpt and a short mapping table. If you want I can follow up with a worked example using your volume numbers and our suggested discount tiers.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, GTM Solutions
Redwood Inference

Hi Alex / Priya — following up with the clarified mapping and a worked example attached. Key points for procurement and forecasting: 

- Mapping summary (short):
  * Responses: billed per input token + per output token (canonical).
  * Chat Completions: billed as Responses; when streaming, output tokens are billed as they are emitted. If you rely on prefix reuse (system + recent messages), those prefixes are billed on first call and reduced via KV cache on subsequent calls.
  * Legacy /completions: uses historical token mapping; if you keep these calls we'll show a separate line on the invoice. Migration to Responses simplifies forecasting and tends to reduce billed input tokens for multi-turn chat due to better cache behavior.

- Worked example (attached): scenario A (full migration to Responses) vs scenario B (20% legacy). For your 25M input / 40M output estimate: 
  * Scenario A (Responses): billed units = 25M input + 40M output => use rates on attached ratecard v3.
  * Scenario B (20% legacy): add legacy token mapping delta ~+3-6% on total billed units (depends on model & prompt structure).

- Discounts: we recommend offering a tiered commit: 20% off list at $20K/mo commit, 28% off at $30K/mo, and a one-time migration credit (up to $15K) if they commit to migrate legacy calls within 90 days. These brackets align with Rishi's guidance.

Next steps: Vivek will send a redline of the MA incorporating the migration credit and I can schedule a short procurement call.

Best,
